Explore the theoretical and practical aspects of quantum machine learning algorithms.

Apply quantum techniques to real-world problems in image and signal processing.

(I) Demonstrate a solid understanding of quantum mechanics and quantum computing principles.

8253.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CS6504 : Performance Analysis of Computing Systems { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Introduction to Probability Models and Simulation: Probability space, Random variables, Discrete and Continuous distribution: uniform, geometric, exponential, normal distribution etc, System Modeling, Measurement techniques, Experimental design, workload design, Simulations, Data Analysis and Visualization Basics of Modeling: Performance metrics: Bandwidth utilization, throughput, delays, error rate, network reliability etc. Poisson process, Bernoulli splitting, PASTA, and Markov chain theory Queuing Theory: Arrival and service processes, Server disciplines, Queuing networks: Open vs closed networks, M/M/1, M/M/1/K, M/M/m, M/M/m/m. M/G/1 full analysis Simulation and Analysis of Computing Systems: time averages versus ensemble averages, Asymptotic bounds and limit theorems, confidence intervals, generating random variables for simulation, Inspection Paradox, Empirical Workload Measurements: heavy-tailed property, Pareto distributions, self-similarity, heavy-tailed distributions, Applications to Computing Systems: analyze the scheduling algorithms and different computing system based on real-life application.

Course Objective

1 .

Define performance goals for models, methods and algorithms in computational systems. Identify system-specific metrics to evaluate the processor, database, network and server workload performance.
2 .

Employ probability theory and computational statistics to analyze system performance. Apply random variables to model the outcome of random experiments using discrete and continuous probability distributions. Analysis of the system using experimental design.
3 .

Apply the Markovian model to analyze continuous & discrete-time queuing processes.
4 .

Design parameters analytically and experimentally to evaluate system performance. Apply simulation methodology to explore dynamism in system behaviour.

Course Outcome

1 .

After successful completion of the course, students would be able to:
CO1: Inspect and examine the outcome of experiments using various approaches or techniques
CO2: Select and interpret appropriate evaluation techniques, performance metrics and workloads for a system
CO3: Apply and build a Markovian model to develop a system model
CO4: Classify and examine various probability distribution models for a given application and compare the performance of various techniques or algorithms.
CO5: Develop a Markovian model to evaluate continuous & discrete-time queuing process by discussing various queuing models

Sheldon M. Ross, Introduction to Probability Models, Academic Press , 7th Edition

Subject Nature : Theory

Module 1 :

Module 1: Overview of linear algebra: Vector space, Matrices and Matrix Algebra, Introduction: Mathematical optimization, Least-squares and linear programming, Convex optimization, Nonlinear optimization. [5 Hours]

To solve constraint and unconstraint optimization problems.

To learn efficient computational procedures for solving optimization problems.

CO5: Able to analyze and apply optimization algorithms.

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Fundamental concepts of drives (8 classes)
Factors affecting selection of drives, speed-torque characteristics of motors and loads, condition of steady-state stability, transient stability: equal area criterion, dynamics of motor load combination, DC shunt motor and series motor braking methods and speed-torque characteristics in four quadrants, Induction motor: steady-state performance analysis, braking methods, four quadrant speed-torque characteristics, dc and ac dynamic braking, Methods of starting, energy relations during starting and braking, Transients in dc and ac drives

Module 2 :

DC drives (8 classes)
Motor and converter performance parameters, 1-phase full- and semi- converter fed dc shunt and dc series motor, Mathematical analysis of 1-phase converter fed dc motors, 1-phase Dual converter: waveforms, operations with and without circulating current, 3-phase full converter, semi converter and dual converter fed dc drives, Power factor considerations of semi- and full converters, Power factor improvement of phase controlled converters, Sequence control of converters, Chopper controlled dc drives, closed loop controlled dc drives, PLL controlled dc drives

Module 3 :

Induction motor drives (10 classes)
Static speed control of induction motor: stator voltage control, Static control of rotor resistance, Static slip power recovery scheme, VSI and cyclo-converter fed drives, V/f control, constant torque and constant power operations, closed loop V/f control, CSI fed drives Induction motor behavior with non-sinusoidal supply and unbalanced supply, PWM inverters and reduction of harmonics

Module 4 :

Synchronous motor drives (6 classes)
Synchronous motor drives: Steady-state performance analysis, braking methods, VSI fed synchronous motor drives, V/f control, true synchronous mode, self synchronous mode, Brushless dc motor drive
Module 5 :

Traction drives (4 classes)
Electric traction services, nature of traction load, main line and sub-urban train configuration, traction mechanics, traction drives, braking, power factor and harmonics, traction motor

At the end of the course, students will be able to apply static control techniques to dc drives

At the end of the course, students will be able to analyze control of induction motor drives

At the end of the course, students will be able to analyze control of synchronous motor drives

8765.t: ID2108: Elements and Principles of Design
8765.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : ID2108 : Elements and Principles of Design { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Introduction to Basic Elements of Design – Line, texture, colour, form, symmetry, balance, scale, mass, unity and variety.
Module 2 :

Concepts of Visual Language and Design – Visual design principles, Gestalt Laws, composition, figure-ground relationship, and negative space.
Module 3 :

Symmetry and Pattern Generation – Use of symmetry, generation of patterns and textures using simple elements.
Module 4 :

Typography and Graphic Composition – Introduction to typography and fonts, use of grids in graphic composition.
Module 5 :

Color Theory and Applications – Colour circle, colour combinations and dimensions (hue, value, chroma), colour meanings in traditions, and psychological use of colours.

Course Objective

1 .

To introduce students to the fundamental elements and principles of design, enabling them to understand and apply concepts like line, texture, color, form, and composition in visual contexts.
2 .

To develop analytical skills for evaluating visual designs, including Gestalt principles, symmetry, and figure-ground relationships, in everyday and professional environments.
3 .

To explore pattern generation, typography, grids, and color theory, fostering the ability to create unified and varied compositions.
4 .

To examine the cultural, psychological, and communicative implications of design choices, particularly in color and visual hierarchy, for effective design solutions.
5 .

To synthesize typography, grid systems, and color theory principles to develop cohesive design solutions that effectively communicate intended messages across various media formats.

Course Outcome

1 .

Students will be able to critically assess visual designs in their everyday environment, articulating how the interaction of various design principles contributes to the effectiveness of the communication.
2 .

Students will be able to analyze and articulate the fundamental elements of design (line, texture, color, form) and their relationships in both historical and contemporary visual compositions.
3 .

Students will be able to generate complex patterns and textures using basic design elements, demonstrating their ability to manipulate symmetry, scale, and repetition to create unified yet varied compositions.
4 .

Students will be able to evaluate the psychological and cultural implications of color choices in design work, incorporating this understanding to create culturally sensitive and emotionally resonant visual compositions.
5 .

Students will be able to apply Gestalt principles and figure-ground relationships to create effective visual hierarchies in their design work.
6 .

Students will be able to synthesize typography, grid systems, and color theory principles to develop cohesive design solutions that effectively communicate intended messages across various media formats.

Essential Reading

1 .

David A. Lauer, Stephen Pentak, Design Basics, Cengage Learning , A foundational text presenting art and design fundamentals in accessible two- to four-page spreads, covering elements like line, texture, color, and form, along with principles such as balance, unity, and composition; ideal for beginners to refer to while working on projects

2 .

Josef Albers, The Interaction of Color, Yale University Press , A classic exploration of color theory through exercises and examples, focusing on how colors interact, their relativity, and perceptual effects; essential for understanding hue, value, chroma, and psychological implications

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Noël Riley, The Elements of Design, Mitchell Beazley , A practical encyclopedia tracing design trends and stylistic elements in decorative arts from the Renaissance to the present, with thematic chapters on forms, patterns, and visual elements; useful for historical context and inspiration

2 .

Josef Müller-Brockmann, Grid Systems in Graphic Design, Niggli Verlag , A visual communication manual detailing the use of grids for typographers, graphic designers, and three-dimensional designers; provides practical guidance on structured composition and layout

Journal and Conferences

1 .

International Journal of Art & Design Education – A peer-reviewed journal focusing on art and design pedagogy, including studies on elements and principles of design.
The Design Journal – An international publication exploring design theory, practice, and visual principles in graphic and industrial design.
International Conference on Design Principles & Practices – An annual conference discussing design education, visual communication, and innovative practices.
